title: Profile Overview
description: Start with the README to understand this repository's purpose: an applied-AI engineering profile backed by selected work, outcomes, and generated visual assets. It also shows where repository cards and activity graphics appear in the public profile, providing context for the automation explored next.

title: Repository Card Generator
description: The card generator is the primary executable component: it fetches GitHub repository metadata and produces themed SVG cards for the README. Its broad fan-out makes it the best code-level map of how repository-list input becomes published profile output.

title: Input And API
description: The generator begins by parsing the curated repository list, then builds GitHub REST endpoints and retrieves metadata with retry handling. This separates user-maintained selection from remote API access before any presentation work begins.
languageLesson: Python dataclasses model immutable values such as repository metadata, while urllib keeps the GitHub request path within the standard library.

title: Card Rendering
description: Repository responses become RepoInfo values and theme settings before SVG rendering formats each card. Text wrapping and HTML escaping protect the generated markup from malformed descriptions while keeping fixed visual bounds.

title: Automation Workflows
description: GitHub Actions schedules the repository-card generator and separately refreshes statistics and contribution visualizations. These workflows turn the profile from a static README into a maintained set of public artifacts without embedding runtime application services.
languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows use triggers to start jobs and ordered steps to run scripts or third-party actions before publishing generated assets.

title: Contribution Standards
description: The contribution guide sets expectations for focused changes, local validation, security reporting, and respectful participation. Read it with the conduct policy and security policy to understand the repository's maintenance boundaries before proposing a change.

title: History And Analysis
description: The changelog records user-facing evolution, while Graphify's report documents an independent generated view of repository structure. Together they distinguish maintained project history from disposable analysis output and make later automation changes easier to audit.
